name: NAGA
lead: The most complete disclosure of trading conditions in our comparison, built-in copy trading with a real leaderboard, and the only one of the five brokers where the whole path from registration to a real account is shown below, step by step.

processes.label: Registration
needed: Email, or sign in with Facebook/Apple
Under a minute — the form is a single screen

items.caption: Fill in the form: name, email, password. Country and phone code are detected automatically by IP.
Right under the "Sign up" button — a short line about the regulator, before you submit the form.

blocks.register_note: The company is in the register as an active Securities Dealer. The register doesn't publish the SD026 number itself — that's only from the broker's own statement.
blocks.quote: «The website is operated by NAGA Capital Ltd which is authorised and regulated by the Financial Services Authority Seychelles (FSA) under licence No. SD026.»
blocks.confirm_note: The entity is named twice: right on the registration form, and in full in the site's footer. Right next to it, on a separate line, a second group entity — NAGA Markets Europe Ltd (CySEC 204/13) — is explicitly labelled "other group entity": not the one running the site for clients from the CIS and Europe.
missing: a compensation fund — not a single mention in the contract, the only avenue for complaints is the Seychelles regulator itself
a published percentage of losing accounts
a numeric leverage cap in policy — only examples (1:300, 1:200), gold advertised up to 1:500

processes.label: Account activation
processes.intro: After registering, open the dashboard — the account already exists. Before trading, fill in a short questionnaire: it unlocks higher limits and is required for verification.

items.caption: Click "Get Started" on the "Set Up Your Live Account" prompt — it takes a couple of minutes.
Enter your details exactly as in your passport: name, date of birth, nationality. You'll also be asked separately whether you're a politically exposed person (PEP) and a US tax resident.
A separate questionnaire ("Financial Details") asks about employment, industry, and trading experience, then source of funds, investment goal, income, and total net worth.
items.note: It also asks which country your deposits and withdrawals will come from, and your Tax Identification Number (TIN) — if your country doesn't issue one, there's a separate answer option for that.

blocks.title: The account becomes "real" after the questionnaire
blocks.body: Right after filling it in, the dashboard sends a "You upgraded to a real-money account!" notification — that's not the same thing as identity verification (see the section below), just confirmation that basic data has been accepted and funding methods are available.

items.caption: In "Funds" → "Deposit", choose a method — card (Visa/Mastercard), Skrill, Neteller, or bank transfer — and enter an amount.

blocks.title: "Withdrawable" isn't the same as your balance
blocks.body: The amount available for withdrawal can be less than what's sitting in the account: if you have open positions, you can only withdraw an amount that would keep your margin level above 150% — otherwise the system won't let you submit the request, to protect you from forced position closures.

processes.label: Verification
processes.intro: Without identity verification, NAGA lets you fund the account up to €2,000 — that figure is stated right on the screen where verification starts, before the process even begins. The check itself is performed by a third-party service, Sumsub, not by NAGA directly.

items.caption: Click "Agree and continue" on the consent screen — it explains that Sumsub processes the data, and gives links to the privacy policy.
An optional step: you can create a Sumsub ID so you don't have to verify again on other services that also use Sumsub.
items.note: The toggle is on by default — if you don't want your data reused, turn it off before clicking "Start verification".

items.caption: Step 1 of 2: choose the country that issued your document and its type — passport, ID card, or driving licence.
items.note: There's a "Continue on phone" button — you can scan a QR code and complete the step with your phone's camera if you don't trust your computer's.

items.caption: Before uploading — three short requirements: a colour photo, good lighting, no edited images.
Attach a file (JPG, PNG, HEIC, WEBP, or PDF, up to 50 MB) or photograph the document right here.
Step 2 of 2 — a liveness check: the system captures your face and background through the camera to confirm the document's owner is the one submitting it.

blocks.title: If the camera won't turn on
blocks.body: Sumsub shows instructions right on the screen: open the site icon in the browser's address bar → find "Camera" → enable access → come back and click "Try again". In automated or isolated browser environments (for example, virtual machines without a physical camera), camera access is technically unavailable — in that case, "Continue on phone" is the only option left.

items.caption: In "Markets", instruments are grouped by category — indices, forex, commodities, crypto — with a live price and the day's change.
"Positions" shows open, pending, and closed trades — before your first trade, it's empty, with a "Start Trading" button.
Open an instrument — a ticket appears on the right: Sell/Buy, market or specific price, volume in lots or an amount in dollars.
items.note: "Order Protector" is Stop Loss and Take Profit, both off by default (toggles on the right). Without a Stop Loss, a position has no limit on losses beyond the account balance.

blocks.title: Margin level is explained right in the interface
blocks.body: Formula: (Equity ÷ Margin used) × 100. Below 50%, NAGA starts force-closing positions — starting with the most unprofitable one, until there's enough margin. Between 51% and 150% — a warning and a recommendation to fund the account or close some positions. Above 150% — everything's fine.

blocks.title: The best disclosure of conditions among the five
blocks.body: NAGA publishes in a single table what the others either don't publish at all or split across pages: long and short swap, average spread in pips, margin, commission, lot size, and volume limits.

blocks.caption: "Hours & Fees" page, checked 2026-08-06. First rows shown as confirmation; the table is alphabetical and loads in batches.

blocks.title: A note on symbols
blocks.body: In the terminal, instruments carry a _Pro suffix: EURUSD_Pro, XAUUSD_Pro. And the DAX 40 index is labelled GER30 (DAX) — the ticker is ten stocks behind the index.

blocks.title: Ready-made signals from Trading Central
body: The "Trading Signals" section has ideas from Trading Central (the same third-party provider AvaTrade uses): instrument, direction, target levels, and a short plain-language scenario.

The base tier gets 5 signals a day — seeing more requires Silver Trader status. Just as with AvaTrade, this isn't our recommendation: the signals are generated automatically by Trading Central's own methodology and are equally available to all clients at the relevant tier.

blocks.title: Built-in copy trading with a public leaderboard
body: "Find Leaders" shows a real trader ranking by profit over the past 30 and 7 days — with follower and copier counts for each. The "Autocopy" button connects you to automatically copy a specific trader's trades.

This isn't a guarantee of results: a leader's past performance promises nothing about the future, and the profit shown is the leader's own profit, not a guaranteed profit for the copier (fees and copy delay reduce it).

blocks.title: You can also earn from your own followers
blocks.body: "Copy Premium" in the "Wallet" section pays the trader being copied — up to $0.90 per lot on popular assets at the Diamond tier. Conditions: be at least Iron tier, trade your own account (not through copying), hold the trade longer than 5 minutes, invest more than $100 in it, and close it in profit. The tier depends on your account balance — starting from zero, it only becomes available after a deposit of $250 or more.
